title: Paper Kitchen: annotated reads + practical next steps
content:
Goal: quick annotated summaries for 6 readings from the last two weeks + concrete experiments to try on the dev cluster. Intent is operational: pick 2 small spikes we can run in a week that will inform batching/kv-cache heuristics for short/medium sessions. Notes are messy — scratchpad style.

1) Paper: "Fast Sparse KV Compression for Long-Context LMs" (workshop draft).
- Key idea: chunked bloom-compression on dense KV blocks with light-weight error-correction; focuses on low-latency decompression path on GPU.
- Why it matters for Redwood: reduces KV memory footprint per active convo, which could allow higher per-GPU concurrency without hurting hot-token latency.
- Repro notes: authors report 1.3–1.6x throughput improvement at 8k context on A100 with negligible perplexity increase when pruning <12% of tokens.
- Open Qs: how stable is perf across variable sequence lengths? Would on-device decompression amplify worst-case latency?
- Quick experiment: implement a toy pass in the runtime that compresses KV by 8:1 with a tiny CUDA kernel (or simulate in CPU first) and measure median/95th token latency for 2,4,8k workloads. Link to spike ticket: RI-2345.

2) Blog: "Streaming-first interfaces for LLM apps" (engineering blog).
- Notes: recommends early tokens as partial responses + chunked reranks. Emphasis on predictable incremental latencies and backpressure.
- Practical: add a streaming mode to the hosted API that emits prefix deltas for deterministic decoders. Need to surface per-chunk latency in console.
- Spike: add a middleware to SDK that reorders/merges partial events and measure client-side latency/UX with react demo app.

3) ICML talk: "Adaptive quantization schedules for on-the-fly lowbit inference"
- Idea: model-selective quant at layer granularity based on activation distributions; low overhead profiling pass at model load.
- Why: we can push more model variants into Dedicated pools if we can trade bitwidth adaptively rather than statically.
- To try: instrument loader to collect per-layer activation variance on a standard sample (wikitext+internal prompts) and compute simple heuristic for per-layer 4/8-bit. Compare quality vs static 8-bit. Ticket: github PR draft linked.

4) Paper cluster: "Eviction strategies for episodic caches"
- Short notes: LRU variants fail when access patterns are bursty; frequency decays and TTL-aware eviction helps.
- Idea for Redwood: combine prefix-aware TTL with frequency counters per-conversation; evict low-utility prefixes older than N tokens.
- Experiment: replay 5000 user traces (prod-sample) with simulated TTL policies and measure hit-rate & extra compute.

5) Mini-survey: "Retrieval augmentation for short-turn contexts" (collection of blog posts/papers).
- Takeaway: for short contexts (<=512) light retrieval with dense-sim scoring gives strong factuality gains with small latency hit. Good candidate for Hosted default in certain routes.

6) Workshop notes: "Fallback policies and graceful degradation"
- Takeaway: explicit routing policy layers that encode semantic compatibility (model fingerprint) -> easier automatic fallback. Also a checklist for per-route fallbacks.
- Action: add a per-route metadata blob that enumerates compatible fallback model ids + expected latency multiplier. Console should surface it.

Actionable next steps (week 1 spikes):
- Spike A (Eliot): KV compress toy: simulate 8:1 compression on CPU KV cache and measure end-to-end median/95th latency for synthetic 2k/8k sessions. (3 days)
- Spike B (Dara): Load profiler for per-layer activation stats; compute naive quant heuristic and run quality checks on dev quant-variants. (3-4 days)
- UX spike (Harper): SDK streaming middleware + react demo; measure front-end perceived latency. (2 days)

Open questions / notes to self:
- Need to sanity-check copyright / licensing for the KV compression algorithm if we reuse ideas.
- If compression kernerls are expensive to decompress at token time we lose latency SLOs; want amortized decompression or async prefetch of chunks.
- Consider measuring cost per-conv-month with compression vs extra throughput; prepare a simple unit-econ calc for next sync.

Links / references (short):
- workshop draft (authors repo): https://example.com/fast-kv-compress
- streaming blog: https://engineering.blog/streaming-llms
- ICML talk slides: https://icml.cc/2026/sessions/quant-adaptive
- Prod sample traces (internal): https://storage.redwood/prod-samples/conv-traces-2026-07
- Spike ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RI-2345

Notes to collaborator: Eliot — please drop any quick numbers in the ticket. Harper — I sketched the react demo flow in the slack thread linked above. Will summarize results next Thursday.
